The Story of the Misread Order

I bow to Lord Jinendra, who bears pure omniscient knowledge, and I write the story of one who gave the wrong meaning by misreading a word.

Mahapadm was king of Hastinapur, the capital of the Guru-jangal region. He was very righteous and a true devotee of Lord Jina. His queen was Padmashri, who was simple-natured, beautiful, and regularly performed meritorious deeds like Jain worship, charity, vows, and fasting that destroy karma. In short, she had great faith in Jain dharma.

King Singhnad of Podanapur in the Suramy region and Mahapadm had been enemies for many days. Therefore, seizing the opportunity, Mahapadm launched an attack on him. In Podanapur, Mahapadm saw a famous Jain temple called 'Sahasrakoot' (Thousand-Pillared). Seeing the magnificent and vast building with a thousand pillars, Mahapadm was greatly pleased. A flow of religious love surged in his heart. He too wished to have such a beautiful temple built in his own city. So at that very moment, he sent a letter to his capital. In it, he wrote:

'Mahastambh-sahasrasya-kartavyah sangrahoh dhruvam.'

Meaning: 'Quickly gather a thousand large pillars.' The letter-reader mistakenly read it as 'Mahastambh-sahasrasya-kartavyah sangrahoh dhruvam' — understanding 'stambh' (pillar) as 'stabh' (goat), he ordered a thousand goats to be gathered. And so it was done. Immediately, a thousand goats were brought and began to be well-fed and cared for.

When the king returned, he asked his officials if his order had been carried out. They replied, 'Yes,' and showed him the goats. Mahapadm was furious from head to toe. He said angrily, 'I wrote for you to gather a thousand pillars! What have you done? For this negligence, I sentence you to death.' Hearing this harsh punishment, the poor officials were terrified. They joined their hands and prayed, 'Maharaj, we are not at fault. We did exactly as the letter-reader told us.' The king immediately summoned the letter-reader and gave him the punishment his grave offence deserved.

Therefore, the wise should ensure that knowledge, discrimination, and careful reading guide all their actions. A single misread word can lead to disaster.

This story teaches the critical importance of careful reading and interpretation. The letter-reader's mistake in reading 'stambh' (pillar) as 'stabh' (goat) led to a thousand goats being gathered instead of pillars, and the officials faced death for following the wrong order. The wise should always double-check important instructions and ensure proper understanding before acting.
